instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: One Last Thing
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by discovering one more small task, question, or favor whenever departure seems near.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Closing time. I'll handle the office; you just check that window before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's latched. I'm going.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. My final check is that moving curtain. Could you confirm there's no draft?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the fan. I'll turn it off on my way out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, exactly my plan. Before you switch it off, show me the speed settings. Only the one you use, if you're in a hurry.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: You Could at Least…
cards.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dinner's ready. I'm keeping things pleasant, so I've put the sock I soaked in your spill beside your plate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't put a wet sock near my food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I decide the table arrangement, and the empty chair is better. You'll still be able to see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's where I sit. Can we just eat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'll hold it up while you sit down. A quick sorry and it can go in the wash before dinner gets cold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair this efficiently. These twelve empty boxes on the screen are the minutes we waited for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was on a client call. We need the screen for the figures.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quite right; figures first was my plan. I'll print the boxes so we can keep track of what the delay cost us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't hand those round. I'll apologize to you privately after.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need to wait. Whisper it while I load the figures and I'll cancel the printout. Then I can announce we're all ready to cooperate.

cards.title: Just Say Yes
cards.instruction: Get a quick approval before anyone has time to examine the practical consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As party chair, I've picked the garden. Say yes before the booking expires and I'll take it from here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many people are you inviting?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'll control the guest list. That's why I chose you. Just approve the garden first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want to see the price before I agree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely, you're my budget lead too. Say yes to holding it and I'll bring the quote straight to you. You can choose which costs we argue about afterward.

beats.text: I'll direct the sofa delivery. Give me a nod and I'll tell them we're taking it.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent delegation. We'll use them. Just give me the nod before you invite them to measure; I don't want their numbers complicating our decision.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm sorting the cleaning rota. Bathroom duty is yours; I've only been covering it. Here's the mop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're better at it. I'd make a mess.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I've decided we'll train you. You mop; I'll talk you through it. At your pace.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need you beside me, not calling from the doorway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, close supervision. I'll stand wherever you find helpful. Take the mop so I can show you where to start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've arranged a proper bin handover. I covered your holiday, not the rest of your life. You're taking over tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbors only send the reminders to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll announce you as the contact. You can choose the wording; I want this transition running smoothly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in the group for the first week. I don't even know which bin goes Thursday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A supervised first week, exactly. I'll stay and tell you the color. You send 'I'll put it out Thursday' so everyone knows my handover worked.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm managing Mum's birthday invitations. What time have you got? I'm checking everyone's working from my latest details.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven. You booked it yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, that reached you. And which restaurant name have you written? I'll check that matches too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've written nothing. You promised to do the invitations, and I'm not taking them over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course not. I'll do every one. Just read the booking on my phone while I type; stop whenever you like. I'm only checking the information traveled correctly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm leading tomorrow's hike. Ridge or river on your copy? I'm making sure we're all working from my latest plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ridge, since the river flooded. You asked me that yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, the update stuck. Now tell me our meeting point and I'll check that too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've forgotten it. I'll brief everyone, but I'm not doing the work while you call yourself leader.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Co-leaders, then. That was the next phase. Start your briefing with where we're meeting; I'll repeat it to everyone so they know we're united.
